paper.title: On Language Generation in the Limit with Bounded Memory
paper.summary: Studies semantic language generation and identification with memoryless, sliding-window, adaptive-buffer, and last-output incremental memory. The registry separates faithful generic interfaces and finite-state obstructions from natural-number-only universal theorems, target-specific density-order games, and source-only fixed-order, countable-family, and comparison claims.

formalization_scope.summary: The complete custom twenty-eight-card surface has nine fully covered claim groups, sixteen partially covered groups, and three source-only groups. Generic no-history, window, buffer, and last-guess interfaces; the output separations; symmetric-chain decomposition; finite-window compactness; finite-state obstructions; and finite-family approximate identification are strongest. Universal countable-universe theorems, fixed-global-order density claims, full Sperner, countable-density and identification extensions, and quantitative comparison corollaries remain incomplete.
specializations: Theorem 1.1, most Section 4 density results, and Appendix A element coding are stated over the paper's arbitrary countable universe but their end-to-end Lean theorems are specialized to natural numbers; no common transport theorem is registered.

The paper fixes one ambient canonical order before choosing the family. Lean quantifies over a separate OrderedLanguage realization of each target after strategy choice; positive guarantees are order-robust, while hard instances may choose a convenient order. This changes the literal minimax game.

MemorylessSetGenerator is a raw function into sets. Eventual validity and the explicit positive witnesses impose infinitude, but the base output codomain does not intrinsically require every output to be infinite.

Theorem 5.2 returns an equal-range topological relabeling rather than a learner conjugated back to the raw input indexing. This is faithful to the paper's extensional collection claim but not a direct raw-index API theorem.
The Appendix A incremental element generator deliberately uses an unbounded natural-valued output as a complete-history code. It is not a finite-bit-memory or machine-space theorem.

All generators and learners are deterministic semantic functions with family-wide static data and classical choice. No endpoint establishes computability, oracle complexity, runtime, convergence rates, randomness, or probability guarantees.
The source indexes a width-W window by its final round; Lean indexes by its first position. The fixed W-1 shift preserves eventual success and the outer limsup.
gaps: A family-wide eventual-success predicate for full-history element generation, the full-history set- and index-output interfaces, and Theorem 3.1's one-example full-memory formulation are absent.
The fixed-global-order versions of Theorems 4.1, 4.2, 4.10, and their hard-instance lemmas are not packaged; the registered equalities compute a related order-robust/adversarial-order game.
Fact 4.5's full maximum-antichain theorem is not a P31 endpoint; only the middle-layer consequence used by the hard construction is present.
Remark 4.9, the other three temporal density aggregates and their collapse claims, and a named adaptive-buffer versus memoryless comparison are source-only.
The countable finite-predecessor extension of Theorem 5.2 and the weak-Angluin obstruction are source-only.
No generic countable-universe transport is registered for the universal natural-number theorems, including the repaired Lemma A.3 wrapper.
No endpoint upgrades semantic bounded example-token memory into bit-bounded, effective, or complexity-certified computation.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Twenty-eight claim groups: full-history generation interfaces; Definition 3, Definition 6, and Theorem 1.1; Theorems 3.1--3.2; Definitions 8--10 with Lemmas 4.3--4.4 and Theorem 4.2; Facts 4.5--4.6; Lemmas 4.7--4.8 and Theorem 4.1; Remark 4.9 plus the temporal-density claims; Definition 11 with Lemma 4.11, Lemma 4.12, and Theorem 4.10; Definition 12 with Theorem 4.15 and Remarks 4.16--4.17; Definitions 13--15, Proposition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, and its countable-family prose; Proposition A.2, Theorem A.1, Lemma A.3, and Theorems A.4--A.5.
exclusions: Definitions 1--2, Remark 2.1, and Example 2.2 are background or illustration; Definition 5 is retained because its three output interfaces delimit P31's Theorem 3.1 and Appendix claims.
Informal Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are crosswalk labels folded into Theorems 4.1, 4.10, 4.15, and 5.2 rather than duplicate cards.
Definition 7 is a taxonomy folded into the memoryless, window, and buffer interface cards. Definitions 9's window/buffer variants are covered with their corresponding theorem cards.
Remarks 4.13--4.14 are explanatory consequences of Lemma 4.12 and are folded into that card. Observation 5.3 and Claims 5.4--5.5 are proof-support steps folded into Theorem 5.2.

Proof-only constructions and subordinate lemmas are excluded when a canonical paper-shaped endpoint exists; source-visible constructions are retained only when they materially specify the claimed learner or generator.
Open questions about computation, oracle access, and further bounded-memory characterizations are recorded as scope boundaries, not promoted to additional conjecture cards.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for this twenty-eight-card claim-centered scope, including all numbered primary results, the numbered order-theory facts, essential interfaces, and substantive source-only extensions. Page locators use printed paper pages; the pinned author PDF has two leading pages, so PDF page numbers are printed page plus two.

Almost containment and almost equivalence mean finite one-sided and symmetric set difference, and a family is incrementally approximately identifiable when one learner eventually keeps every hypothesis almost equivalent to the target on every exact presentation.

source_assessment.notes: These definitions fix the last-index-only access restriction and extensional finite-error objective used by Proposition 5.1 and Theorem 5.2.

claims.title: Every finite collection is incrementally identifiable up to finite error
claims.statement_summary: Every finite collection of infinite languages admits one last-guess incremental learner whose hypotheses are eventually almost equivalent to the target on every exact positive presentation; after topologically ordering strict almost-containment, the learner stays when the current example belongs to its current hypothesis and otherwise advances by one, capped at the final index.

source_assessment.notes: Finite candidate order ensures only finitely many irreversible advances and leaves finite symmetric error with the target.

formalization.notes: Lean formalizes the stay-or-advance construction and the extensional finite-family theorem. Its equal-range relabeling is faithful to the source's set-family semantics and does not assert preservation of arbitrary duplicate indices.

claims.title: The finite-family argument has a finite-predecessor extension and a weak-Angluin boundary
claims.statement_summary: The paper remarks that incremental approximate identification extends to countable families whose strict almost-containment order has a suitable topological enumeration with finitely many predecessors per target, while violation of the weak Angluin condition prevents approximate identification even with full information.

source_assessment.notes: The positive extension is stated informally with a 'suitable' topological-order proviso, and the negative boundary is attributed to prior weak-Angluin results rather than proved here.

formalization.notes: No P31 declaration states either the countable finite-predecessor theorem or the imported full-information obstruction.

claims.title: Finite collections admit pairwise disjoint infinite cofinal coding cells
claims.statement_summary: For every finite collection of infinite languages over the canonically ordered countable universe, each language contains an infinite cofinal subset and these selected subsets can be made pairwise disjoint.

source_assessment.notes: The recursive diagonal selection avoids all earlier choices and selects a later point from each infinite language at every stage.

formalization.notes: The repaired wrapper packages all four source properties over Nat. It postdates the immutable AI comparison audit, is kernel-checked, and remains pending human correspondence review; arbitrary countable ordered universes remain uncovered.

claims.title: An eventually almost-contained full-history learner compiles to incremental element generation
claims.statement_summary: For a finite collection of infinite languages, any full-information index learner whose hypotheses are eventually almost contained in every target can be compiled into an incremental element generator: the previous output encodes the complete observed prefix and current hypothesis, and future outputs are fresh target elements.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem is explicitly conditional on a substantive full-history learner; cofinal disjoint coding cells let one natural-valued action carry the entire finite history without claiming finite-bit memory.

formalization.notes: Lean exposes the one-sided premise, the explicit Nat history-code construction, and the conditional compiler with exact causal arity and freshness. The arbitrary countable-universe theorem is not registered.

claims.title: Every finite collection admits incremental element generation via last-output history coding
